title: Review of lab 1's fl_morph257 (I) on fresh seeds 5 and 6: from one noise patch, two body plans (rings and crescents) form within ~50 t and individual bodies live hundreds of t between collisions, though labkit's tracks churn (merges ~ splits)
summary: labkit re-runs of threads/flow-lenia/worlds/fl_morph257/world.py on fresh seeds 5 and 6 with the pack's settings (frames 300, spf 20, t=1200, 128^2). From one 12 px noise patch, discrete bodies form by t~50-100 and settle at 13 per run (occupancy 0.15-0.16): small orange rings and cyan multi-segment crescents (rerun/seed5/sheet.png). Several bodies keep their shape for hundreds of t between collisions (e.g. an orange ring at the centre from t~212 to 888, and crescent-ring pairs from t~300 to 600), against a formation time of ~50 t. labkit's identity churn is high: 307/410 tracks, persistent tracks 2/0, splits 105/142 vs merges 99/136, max 2.1/3.8 body lengths (original pack: 462 tracks, 1 persistent, 6.7 BL). Under the RUBRIC L2 rule for colliding populations (a body's lifetime between collisions much longer than its formation time, judged from images) I counts.

observations.I: rerun/seed5/sheet.png: discrete ring and crescent bodies from t~100; an orange ring keeps its shape from t~212 to 888 between collisions

verdicts.limitation: Planted noise patch, one per run. labkit's tracker fragments identities at every collision (persistent tracks 0-2), so I rests on the images. The interaction, motion and division lab 1 mentions were not examined.
